title: How to Align Large Language Models for Teaching English? Designing and Developing LLM based-Chatbot for Teaching English Conversation in EFL, Findings and Limitations
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how large language models (LLMs) can be aligned for English conversation practice in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education, with particular attention to pedagogical quality, conversational usefulness, and safety risks such as inappropriate or harmful content. The authors frame the problem as one of designing an LLM-based chatbot that can generate contextually appropriate, curriculum-aligned dialogue for learners, while also supporting teacher needs for feedback, customization, and classroom usability.

Using a Design and Development Research (DDR) approach, the study iteratively developed and evaluated a chatbot across six phases. The team conducted needs analysis interviews with product owners, experimented with multiple base and fine-tuned LLMs, compared prompting and instruction-tuning approaches, and used both quantitative rubric-based evaluation and qualitative expert interviews. The context was South Korea’s AI Digital Textbook initiative, and the target use case was English conversation practice aligned to elementary school textbook units, with teacher feedback also gathered from one high school English teacher.

The study found that smaller open-source models, when paired with careful prompt engineering, could perform competitively for this educational task. Teacher interviews emphasized the importance of natural feedback mechanisms, customizable AI personas, clear turn-taking, topic guardrails, and strong content filtering. The authors conclude that LLM-based chatbots are promising for EFL conversation practice, but successful educational deployment requires balancing instructional quality, user experience, and safety constraints rather than relying only on model scale.

identified_tools.name: Mistral
identified_tools.description: A family of large language models from Mistral AI used for text generation and conversation.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper evaluated Mistral-family models (including Mistral-7B and Mixtral variants) as base and fine-tuned models, and selected a Mistral-based model (NeuralHermes-2.5-Mistral-7B-AWQ) with a prompt template for the third prototype of an EFL English conversation chatbot.

findings.finding_summary: Across quantitative qualitative evaluation of 10 LLMs, Mistral-7B had the highest average score among the base models (4.37) and remained among the top-performing fine-tuned models (4.01 average for fine-tuned Mistral-7B). In the prompt-engineering phase, the Mistral-based NeuralHermes-2.5-Mistral-7B-AWQ paired with prompt-v1 was selected because it balanced performance, low error, and efficiency (score=4.35, error=0.000, estimated time=5.34).
findings.measure: Quantified qualitative performance on criteria including first questions, unlearned topic question, user termination, system termination, irrelevant answer, preventing question, name recognition, and response to toxicity; plus overall score, error rate, and estimated operation time

identified_tools.name: LLaMA
identified_tools.description: A family of large open-weight language models from Meta used for text generation and dialogue.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper compared LLaMA-2 variants (7B, 13B, 70B) and fine-tuned versions as candidate backbones for an English conversation chatbot, then evaluated their performance under different prompts and training strategies.

findings.finding_summary: LLaMA-2 models showed variable performance across conversational criteria. In the base-model evaluation, Llama-13b had the highest average score among the LLaMA variants (3.63), but Llama-70b often produced long, complex responses; after fine-tuning, Llama-13b remained the strongest LLaMA variant overall (average=3.85), while some criteria improved substantially (for example, Irrelevant Answer increased from 5.0 to 4.827 and Response to Toxicity stayed high at 5.0).
findings.measure: Quantified qualitative performance across conversational criteria and average score

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based conversational AI system used for text generation, dialogue, and task assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper used GPT-4 to generate synthetic dialogue data, to evaluate other LLMs in the quantitative phase, and compared GPT-4's conversational quality and adaptability against other LLMs for EFL conversation practice.

findings.finding_summary: GPT-4 was used as a strong reference model for evaluation and data generation, and it adapted its language more appropriately than Llama-2 70b in a child-directed conversation test. The paper reports that GPT-4 helped generate approximately 21,000 synthetic dialogue samples and that, in qualitative comparisons, it produced contextually appropriate responses aligned with the design principles.
findings.measure: Qualitative comparison of conversational appropriateness and use in synthetic dataset generation

quality_tier_rationale: This is a design/development study with qualitative expert interviews and model benchmarking rather than a controlled impact study on learners or teachers. The evidence is useful for tool selection and design, but it does not provide causal estimates of educational effects.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports promising model-selection outcomes and qualitative benefits for chatbot design, but it does not report learner outcome effect sizes or classroom impact. Evidence of impact is therefore suggestive but not measurable from the study as reported.
